method: S1 is the open RACGP AJGP 2023 review of male sexual dysfunction, fetched and checked verbatim (15 claims, 4 of them dose tables). A1 is AMH across two pages, paraphrased, no passage reproduced and no source_text stored (30 claims, 7 doses). The PDE5 INHIBITOR DOSES ARE QUOTED from the open source, which carries a starting and maximum dose for each agent while AMH's class monograph carries none. S1 covers male sexual dysfunction broadly -- low libido, Peyronie's disease, ejaculatory and orgasmic disorders -- and only its erectile dysfunction and shared-assessment content is used here, because the AMH topic closed is erectile dysfunction. Testosterone regimens are included only where S1 states them for hypogonadism with low libido; hypogonadism is NOT an AMH topic closed here and is not developed.

claims.claim: Erectile dysfunction is defined as difficulty achieving or maintaining an erection, and it is estimated that a third of males will experience one form of male sexual dysfunction in their lifetimes
claims.source_text: Erectile dysfunction is defined as difficulty achieving or maintaining an erection. 3,7-9 … It is estimated that a third of males will experience one form of MSD in their lifetimes.

claims.claim: S1 states that erectile dysfunction serves as an important marker of future cardiovascular risk and that literature has shown the risks of cardiovascular disease and death increase steadily with the severity of erectile dysfunction
claims.source_text: It serves as an important marker of future cardiovascular risk, and literature has shown that the risks of cardiovascular disease and death increase steadily with the severity of erectile dysfunction.

claims.claim: Erectile dysfunction is more common with increasing age and in those with multiple medical comorbidities including metabolic syndrome and chronic medical illness, and there is a strong association between erectile dysfunction and lower urinary tract symptoms or benign prostatic hyperplasia
claims.source_text: Erectile dysfunction is more common with increasing age and in those with multiple medical comorbidities, including metabolic syndrome and chronic medical illness. 2,3,8 It serves as an important marker of future cardiovascular risk, and literature has shown that the risks of cardiovascular disease and death increase steadily with the severity of erectile dysfunction. 3,8 In addition, there is a strong association between erectile dysfunction and lower urinary tract symptoms/benign prostatic hyperplasia.

claims.claim: Male hypogonadism, a pathological disorder of the hypothalamic-pituitary-testicular axis with biochemical low total testosterone, can be associated with cardiometabolic complications and ensuing erectile dysfunction, low libido, delayed ejaculation and anorgasmia
claims.source_text: Male hypogonadism, which is defined as a pathological disorder of the hypothalamic-pituitary-testicular axis and biochemical low total testosterone level, can be associated with cardiometabolic complications and ensuing erectile dysfunction, low libido, delayed ejaculation and anorgasmia.

claims.claim: Patient history remains an integral part of evaluation given these dysfunctions are self-reported conditions and many lack confirmatory diagnostic tests, with emphasis on open dialogue in a face-to-face consultation and sensitivity towards the patient's unique ethnic, cultural and personal background
claims.source_text: Patient history remains an integral part of evaluating patients presenting with MSD given that these dysfunctions represent self-reported conditions and many lack confirmatory diagnostic tests. 1-5,15,17 Emphasis is placed on an open dialogue in a face-to-face consultation and being mindful of the patient's sexual concerns with sensitivity towards the patient's unique ethnic, cultural and personal background.

claims.claim: S1 states that modifying lifestyle behaviours, managing reversible risk factors and optimising existing medical conditions are important first-line management options before pharmacotherapy and should be performed in a holistic, patient-centred approach
claims.source_text: Modifying lifestyle behaviours, managing reversible risk factors and optimising existing medical conditions are important first-line management options before pharmacotherapy (Table 2) and should be performed in a holistic, patient-centred approach.

claims.claim: S1 states that oral phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitor medication remains the standard of care and is considered the first-line pharmacological intervention, and that while often effective, well tolerated and safe when prescribed appropriately, their use should be cautioned in males with unstable angina or currently taking nitrate therapy
claims.source_text: Oral phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5) inhibitor medication remains the standard of care and is considered the first-line pharmacological intervention. 1,3,7,8,19 While PDE5 inhibitor medications are often effective, well tolerated and safe when prescribed appropriately, their use should be cautioned in males with unstable angina or who are currently taking nitrates therapy and follow careful discussion about the pros and cons of medications.

claims.claim: S1 states that for patients with hypogonadism, restoring testosterone levels will improve PDE5 inhibitor efficacy and salvage PDE5 non-responders
claims.source_text: For patients with hypogonadism, restoring testosterone levels will improve PDE5 inhibitor efficacy and salvage PDE5 non-responders.

claims.claim: Intracavernous injection of vasoactive agents such as prostaglandin E1, also known as alprostadil, is recommended as second-line therapy in males who did not respond to oral PDE5 inhibitor treatment, and the prescription should include detailed discussion with the patient consisting of technical instruction and education about priapism
claims.source_text: Intracavernous injection (ICI) of vasoactive agents such as prostaglandin E1 (also known as alprostadil) is recommended as second-line therapy in males who did not respond to oral PDE5 inhibitor treatment, and the prescription of these ICI medications should include a detailed discussion with the patient that consists of technical instruction and education about priapism.

claims.claim: Vacuum constriction devices can provide passive engorgement of the corpora cavernosa with a constriction ring placed at the base of the penis to maintain an erection, and a penile prosthesis implant can be offered following appropriate consultation with a urologist for patients who do not respond to or tolerate PDE5 inhibitors or want more definitive treatment
claims.source_text: Vacuum constriction devices can provide passive engorgement of the corpora cavernosa, and a constriction ring can be placed at the base of the penis to maintain an erection. 7,8,19 For patients who do not respond to or tolerate PDE5 inhibitor medications or are keen on more definitive treatment, a penile prosthesis implant can be offered following appropriate consultation with a urologist.

claims.claim: S1 states that the role of regenerative therapy such as low-intensity shockwave therapy and penile injection of stem cells or platelet-rich plasma is not recommended since these methods lack long-term efficacy and safety records and are not properly regulated by the government
claims.source_text: The role of regenerative therapy, such as low-intensity shockwave therapy and penile injection of stem cells or platelet-rich plasma, is not recommended since these methods lack long-term efficacy and safety records and are not properly regulated by the government.

claims.claim: S1 gives sildenafil as oral therapy 30 minutes before sex with a starting dose of 25 to 50 mg and maximum dose 100 mg, a half-life of approximately four hours, and absorption affected by food and alcohol
claims.source_text: Sildenafil Oral therapy; 30 minutes before sex Starting dose 25-50 mg Maximum dose 100 mg - Medication half-life approximately four hours - Absorption affected by food and alcohol

claims.claim: S1 gives tadalafil as oral therapy 60 minutes before sex with a starting dose of 10 to 20 mg and maximum dose 20 mg, a half-life of approximately 17.5 hours, and absorption not affected by food and alcohol
claims.source_text: Tadalafil Oral therapy; 60 minutes before sex Starting dose 10-20 mg Maximum dose 20 mg - Medication half-life approximately 17.5 hours - Absorption not affected by food and alcohol

claims.claim: S1 gives daily tadalafil as oral therapy at 5 mg for daily use, and avanafil as oral therapy 30 minutes before sex with a starting dose of 100 mg and maximum dose 200 mg
claims.source_text: Tadalafil daily Oral therapy; daily use 5 mg … Avanafil Oral therapy; 30 minutes before sex Starting dose 100 mg Maximum dose 200 mg

claims.claim: S1 gives testosterone 1% gel as one sachet or two pumps daily increasing to two sachets or four pumps as required, testosterone 2% as one pump daily increasing to two pumps as required, and testosterone undecanoate 1000 mg in 4 mL as an intramuscular injection once every three months
claims.source_text: One sachet or two pumps daily (increase to two sachets or four pumps as required) … One pump daily (increase to two pumps as required) … Testosterone undecanoate (1000 mg/4 mL) Intramuscular therapy Once every three monthly

claims.claim: Erectile dysfunction is often due to a combination of organic and psychogenic problems, with organic causes including neurological, vascular, endocrine, structural and drug-induced causes such as beta-blockers and alcohol misuse, while psychogenic causes may respond to counselling or behaviour therapy, and attention to psychological factors is important in all cases

claims.claim: If irreversible organic causes are implicated the 3 main treatments are drug treatment, a vacuum pump which induces erection by negative pressure, and prostheses
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Erectile dysfunction' (Genitourinary drugs > Drugs for sexual dysfunction) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/drugs-sexual-dysfunction/erectile-dysfunction, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states that phosphodiesterase 5 inhibitors, being avanafil, sildenafil and tadalafil, are the drugs of choice due to their effectiveness and ease of use, that onset of effect is about 30 minutes to 1 hour, that they are generally well tolerated, that most clinical experience has been gained with sildenafil, and that they are contraindicated in men taking nitrates

claims.claim: AMH states PDE5 inhibitors should be used alone as safety and efficacy are not well established for combination treatments, although some studies suggest combining alprostadil with sildenafil may be helpful
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Erectile dysfunction' (Genitourinary drugs > Drugs for sexual dysfunction) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/drugs-sexual-dysfunction/erectile-dysfunction, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Alprostadil is effective alone or with other agents and of the injectable products is least likely to cause penile fibrosis or priapism, papaverine may be used alone or in combination but considered only if intracavernosal alprostadil is inappropriate, and phentolamine must be used with papaverine and/or alprostadil injection to be effective
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Erectile dysfunction' (Genitourinary drugs > Drugs for sexual dysfunction) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/drugs-sexual-dysfunction/erectile-dysfunction, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states that continued erection requires aspiration of 20 to 50 mL of blood from the corpus cavernosum via a 19 or 21 gauge butterfly needle, that this may be repeated on the other side if necessary, and that if still unsuccessful urgent urological review is necessary

claims.claim: PDE5 inhibitors act because sexual stimulation increases cyclic GMP causing smooth muscle relaxation and inflow of blood to the corpus cavernosum, and these agents inhibit the breakdown of cyclic GMP by phosphodiesterase 5
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug class monograph 'Phosphodiesterase 5 inhibitors (genitourinary)' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/drugs-sexual-dysfunction/phosphodiesterase-5-inhibitors-genitourinary, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states PDE5 inhibitors are contraindicated with nitric oxide donors, organic nitrates or nitrites including glyceryl trinitrate in any form, isosorbide mononitrate, isosorbide dinitrate, sodium nitroprusside, amyl nitrite and nicorandil, or with riociguat, due to the risk of profound hypotension or myocardial infarction
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug class monograph 'Phosphodiesterase 5 inhibitors (genitourinary)' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/drugs-sexual-dysfunction/phosphodiesterase-5-inhibitors-genitourinary, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug class monograph 'Phosphodiesterase 5 inhibitors (genitourinary)' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/drugs-sexual-dysfunction/phosphodiesterase-5-inhibitors-genitourinary, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH advises that treatment with drugs that can cause hypotension, particularly selective alpha-blockers, may add to hypotension caused by PDE5 inhibitors, and that if using with an alpha-blocker the alpha-blocker therapy should be stabilised before starting the PDE5 inhibitor at the lowest starting dose
